questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Independent Variables?
questions.answer: The independent variable is the input with respect to which derivatives are taken. An ODE uses one independent variable, usually time or one spatial coordinate.

questions.prompt: What does \(t\) mean in Independent Variables?
questions.answer: In Independent Variables, \(t\) means time input. Its unit is s.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Independent Variables.
questions.answer: In Independent Variables, \(x\) means one spatial input. Its unit is m.

questions.prompt: A population P satisfies dP/dt equals rP. Name the independent variable.
questions.answer: The derivative dP/dt means P is differentiated with respect to t. The independent variable is time t, and P(t) is the dependent variable: \[\frac{dP}{dt}=rP\]

questions.prompt: A small deflection y satisfies d squared y over dx squared equals M divided by EI. Name the independent variable.
questions.answer: The derivative is with respect to x, so x is the independent spatial coordinate. The dependent variable is the deflection y(x): \[\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\frac{M}{EI}\]
